Implicit weights from AIPW or regression adjustment with staggered adoption

Source: R/twfeweights_mp.R
implicit_aipw_weights.Rd

Estimates the overall average treatment effect on the treated, \(ATT^o\), by augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW), regression adjustment or inverse probability weighting, and writes each group-time estimate as a reweighting estimator so that aipw_cov_bal() can report how well the implicit weights balance covariates (Caetano and Callaway, 2024).

Usage

implicit_aipw_weights(
  yname,
  tname,
  idname,
  gname,
  xformula = ~1,
  d_covs_formula = NULL,
  pscore_formula = xformula,
  pscore_d_covs_formula = d_covs_formula,
  extra_balance_vars_formula = NULL,
  extra_balance_d_vars_formula = NULL,
  balance_d_vars_post = TRUE,
  data,
  weightsname = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

yname

Name of the outcome variable.

tname

Name of the time period variable.

idname

Name of the unit identifier.

gname

Name of the group variable: the first period a unit is treated, or 0 for never-treated units.

xformula

One-sided formula for covariates in the outcome model. Time-varying covariates enter through their level in the base period (\(g-1\)), as in did::att_gt(); time-invariant covariates can also be included. Default ~1.

d_covs_formula

One-sided formula for time-varying covariates entered through their change from the base period, \(X_t - X_{g-1}\). Default NULL.

pscore_formula

One-sided formula for covariates in the propensity score model. Defaults to xformula. Use ~1 for regression adjustment; use covariates here with xformula = ~1 for inverse probability weighting.

pscore_d_covs_formula

One-sided formula for covariate changes in the propensity score model. Defaults to d_covs_formula.

extra_balance_vars_formula

Ignored; balance is computed afterwards with aipw_cov_bal(). Present so the arguments match two_period_aipw_weights().

extra_balance_d_vars_formula

Ignored, as for extra_balance_vars_formula.

balance_d_vars_post

Ignored, as for extra_balance_vars_formula.

data

A panel data.frame in long format. Unbalanced panels are balanced first (with a warning about the rows dropped).

weightsname

Name of the column holding sampling weights, which must be constant over time within each unit. Default NULL (unweighted).

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class decomposed_aipw: a list with est (the estimate of \(ATT^o\)), aipw_gt (one element per post-treatment \((g,t)\) cell with g and tp on a 1, 2, ..., T scale, the estimate est, the cell's weight in \(ATT^o\) att_weight, the implicit weights, dy, D and the comparison group's effective sample size ess), and the inputs needed by aipw_cov_bal().

Details

For each treated group \(g\) and post-treatment period \(t\), two_period_aipw_weights() is applied to group \(g\) and the never-treated group in periods \(g-1\) and \(t\). The \(ATT(g,t)\) are then combined into \(ATT^o\) with the weights in attO_weights(). Without d_covs_formula, the results equal did::att_gt() with the never-treated comparison group and the same covariates, aggregated with did::aggte(type = "group"). Regression adjustment (pscore_formula = ~1) is often preferable when groups are small, since the propensity score can then be poorly estimated.

References

Caetano, Carolina and Brantly Callaway. "Difference-in-Differences when Parallel Trends Holds Conditional on Covariates." Working paper (2024). doi:10.48550/arXiv.2406.15288

Callaway, Brantly and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna. "Difference-in-Differences with Multiple Time Periods." Journal of Econometrics 225.2 (2021). doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.12.001

See also

aipw_cov_bal(), summary.decomposed_aipw(), implicit_twfe_weights().

Examples

data(castle, package = "causaldata")
castle <- as.data.frame(castle)
castle$G <- BMisc::get_group(castle, "sid", tname = "year", treatname = "post")

# regression adjustment
ra <- implicit_aipw_weights(
  yname = "l_homicide", tname = "year", idname = "sid", gname = "G",
  xformula = ~l_police, pscore_formula = ~1, data = castle
)
